purpose: Central evidence register for all production concepts, including claim-level peer-review sources and source-linked foundational references.

reviewPolicy.primaryRule: Use the highest-quality source appropriate to the claim; guidelines for clinical recommendations, systematic reviews/meta-analyses for synthesis, specialist texts for stable foundations, and primary studies when synthesis is unavailable.
reviewPolicy.uncertaintyRule: Distinguish established findings, emerging evidence, theoretical models, contested claims and superseded claims.
reviewPolicy.copyrightRule: Store citations, identifiers, summaries and links; do not reproduce copyrighted source text or figures.
reviewPolicy.releaseGate: Every production concept must resolve to evidence-review metadata and at least one Evidence Library source. Higher-risk clinical, diagnostic, treatment, biomarker and contested-mechanism content requires explicit boundaries plus current guideline/systematic-review evidence where available.
reviewPolicy.futureContentRule: No new factual concept content is release-ready until its evidence-review record and source links are updated.

sources.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Post-traumatic stress disorder (NG116). Published 2018; last reviewed 8 April 2025.
sources.evidenceStrength: high for treatment recommendations
sources.limitations: Guideline recommendations support treatment decisions; they do not establish a unique neural mechanism for EMDR or other therapies.

sources.citation: World Health Organization. Post-traumatic stress disorder fact sheet.
sources.evidenceStrength: high-level authoritative summary
sources.limitations: Summary-level source; use primary reviews/guidelines for detailed comparative-effectiveness claims.

sources.citation: Wright SL, Karyotaki E, Cuijpers P, et al. EMDR v. other psychological therapies for PTSD: a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis. Psychological Medicine. 2024;54(8):1580-1588. doi:10.1017/S0033291723003446.
sources.sourceType: systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis
sources.evidenceStrength: high
sources.limitations: Only 8 of 15 eligible RCTs contributed participant-level data (346 participants); comparator therapies varied.

sources.citation: Westwood SJ, Aggensteiner P-M, Kaiser A, et al. Neurofeedback for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. JAMA Psychiatry. 2025;82(2):118-129. doi:10.1001/jamapsychiatry.2024.3702.
sources.sourceType: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials
sources.evidenceStrength: high
sources.limitations: Group-level results do not rule out benefit for selected individuals; small effects appeared in analyses restricted to established standard protocols.

sources.citation: Ros T, Enriquez-Geppert S, Zotev V, et al. Consensus on the reporting and experimental design of clinical and cognitive-behavioural neurofeedback studies (CRED-nf checklist). Brain. 2020;143(6):1674-1685.
sources.evidenceStrength: methodological standard
sources.limitations: A reporting/design standard, not evidence that a specific neurofeedback protocol is efficacious.

sources.citation: Rezaee M, Effatpanah M, Nasehi MM, Ghamkhar L, Barati N. Assessing the Impact of Neurofeedback on Cognitive Function in Individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review. Iran J Child Neurol. 2025;19(2):27-37. doi:10.22037/ijcn.v19i2.46578.
sources.evidenceStrength: low-to-moderate
sources.limitations: Only 12 studies were included; protocols and cognitive outcomes were heterogeneous, so efficacy for autism as a condition cannot be inferred.

sources.citation: Gloss D, Varma JK, Pringsheim T, Nuwer MR. Practice advisory: The utility of EEG theta/beta power ratio in ADHD diagnosis. Neurology. 2016;87(22):2375-2379. Reaffirmed by the American Academy of Neurology 18 October 2025. doi:10.1212/WNL.0000000000003265.
sources.evidenceStrength: high for diagnostic-use recommendation
sources.limitations: Addresses theta/beta ratio and frontal beta power as diagnostic aids, not every possible EEG/QEEG research application in ADHD.

sources.citation: Tenney JR, Gloss D, Arya R, et al. Practice Guideline: Use of Quantitative EEG for the Diagnosis of Mild Traumatic Brain Injury. J Clin Neurophysiol. 2021;38(4):287-292. doi:10.1097/WNP.0000000000000853.
sources.evidenceStrength: high for diagnostic-use recommendation
sources.limitations: Specifically addresses qEEG for diagnosing mTBI, including remote diagnosis and differentiation from other conditions.

sources.citation: Grossman P. Fundamental challenges and likely refutations of the five basic premises of the polyvagal theory. Biol Psychol. 2023;180:108589. doi:10.1016/j.biopsycho.2023.108589.
sources.evidenceStrength: substantive critique
sources.limitations: A critical appraisal rather than a neutral consensus statement; should be read alongside responses and proponent accounts.

sources.citation: Grossman P, Ackland GL, Allen AM, et al. Why The Polyvagal Theory Is Untenable: An international expert evaluation of the polyvagal theory. Clin Neuropsychiatry. 2026;23(1):100-112. doi:10.36131/cnfioritieditore20260110.
sources.evidenceStrength: substantive multi-expert critique
sources.limitations: Evaluates foundational neurophysiological/evolutionary premises; it does not test whether state-based metaphors have clinical utility.

sources.citation: Porges SW. Polyvagal Theory: Current Status, Clinical Applications, and Future Directions. Clin Neuropsychiatry. 2025;22(3):169-184. doi:10.36131/cnfioritieditore20250301.
sources.evidenceStrength: theoretical/proponent perspective
sources.limitations: Written by the originator of the theory; not independent validation of its disputed premises.

sources.citation: Porges SW. When A Critique Becomes Untenable: A Scholarly Response To Grossman Et Al.'s Evaluation Of Polyvagal Theory. Clin Neuropsychiatry. 2026;23(1). doi:10.36131/cnfioritieditore20260111.
sources.evidenceStrength: theoretical/proponent response
sources.limitations: A response by the theory originator; documents the live scientific dispute rather than resolving it.

sources.citation: Wright LA, Horstmann L, Holmes EA, Bisson JI. Consolidation/reconsolidation therapies for the prevention and treatment of PTSD and re-experiencing: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Transl Psychiatry. 2021;11:453. doi:10.1038/s41398-021-01570-w.
sources.evidenceStrength: moderate/emerging
sources.limitations: Most included studies had significant risk of bias and only selected reconsolidation/consolidation protocols were superior to controls.

sources.citation: Wadji DL, Martin-Soelch C, Camos V. Can working memory account for EMDR efficacy in PTSD? BMC Psychol. 2022;10(1):245. doi:10.1186/s40359-022-00951-0.
sources.evidenceStrength: moderate for a component mechanism
sources.limitations: Supports dual-task effects on vividness/emotionality but does not establish working-memory taxation as the complete mechanism of clinical EMDR efficacy.

sources.citation: El-Khalil C, Caculidis Tudor D, Nedelcea C. Impact of intergenerational trauma on second-generation descendants: a systematic review. BMC Psychol. 2025;13(1):668. doi:10.1186/s40359-025-03012-4.
sources.evidenceStrength: moderate for associations
sources.limitations: Quantitative observational evidence cannot cleanly separate biological inheritance from family, social, historical and structural pathways.

sources.citation: Biological Embedding of Early-Life Adversity and a Scoping Review of the Evidence for Intergenerational Epigenetic Transmission of Stress and Trauma in Humans. Genes (Basel). 2023;14(8):1639. doi:10.3390/genes14081639.
sources.evidenceStrength: limited/emerging for human intergenerational epigenetic transmission
sources.limitations: Human evidence for epigenetic transmission across generations remains debated and is vulnerable to shared-environment and other confounding.
